subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to see individual summaries of scanone for multiple phenotypes

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to see individual summaries of scanone for multiple phenotypes
parts:
The summary.scanone function doesn't take a pheno.col argument, but rather a lodcolumn argument.
And there will 3*27 lod columns, with lod(p,mu), lod(p), and lod(mu) for each phenotype.

With my brief tests, it seems like summary should work okay. Perhaps try format="tabByChr"

summary(out.2part, perms=perm.2part, alpha=0.05, pvalues=TRUE, format="tabByChr")

Also, maybe try a more conservative type 1 error rate, say alpha=0.2.

karl

> On Dec 18, 2016, at 3:21 PM, Vanessa N <vanessa...@mail.utoronto.ca> wrote:
>
> Dear Karl,
>
> I ran scanones and performed permulations for multiple phenotypes using the following code:
>
> out.2part <- scanone(mydata, pheno.col=c(1:27), model="2part")
> perm.2part <- scanone(mydata, pheno.col=c(1:27), model="2part", n.perm=2500)
> perm.2part.sum <- summary(perm.2part, alpha=c(0.1, 0.05))
>
> I am able to use the following code to plot the LOD score for the phenotypes separately:
>
> for(i in 1:(length(mydata$pheno)-1)){
> plot(out.2part, lodcolumn=(i*3-2))
> abline(h=perm.2part.sum[2,i*3-2],col="black", lty=1)
> abline(h=perm.2part.sum[1,i*3-2],col="grey", lty=2)
> title(main=colnames(mydata$pheno[i]))
> dev.off()
> }
>
> However, I am not able to bring up summaries for the phenotypes separately. I've tried the following code:
>
> summary(out.2part, pheno.col=(21), perms=perm.2part, alpha=0.05, pvalues=TRUE)
>
> It tells me there are no LOD peaks above the threshold, but I know this isn't true based on the plots, and by looking at the scanone results.
> How can I get a summary for individual phenotypes?
>
> Best,
>
> Vanessa
>
